items.prose: Scavenged typography metal from a ruined printing plant yielded an 84/12/4 Pb/Sb/Sn eutectic alloy. Cast 7.62mm rifle bullets measure 22 Brinell hardness; bullets engage rifling cleanly at 2,400 FPS without bore leading or gas blowby.

Clip-on automotive wheel weights melted with 0.5% trace arsenic. Dropping the freshly cast 9mm bullets directly from the steel mold into an ice-water bucket caused age-hardening precipitation, raising Brinell hardness from 12 to 28 BHN within one week.

Using pure un-alloyed roofing flashing lead (5 BHN) to cast high-velocity .308 Winchester rounds resulted in catastrophic barrel leading. After fifteen shots, lead foil completely stripped into the rifling grooves, raising chamber pressure to 65,000 PSI and sticking the bolt.

Melting modern maintenance-free lead-calcium battery plates formed a thick, powdery grey dross that would not flux with beeswax. Trapped calcium oxide inclusions formed spongy porous cavities in cast bullet bases, causing wild 14 MOA accuracy dispersion.

Heavy machinery Babbitt bearing scrap containing 55% tin, 15% antimony, and 5% copper cast into .45-70 flat-nose bullets. The tough copper-tin needle crystals allow the bullets to punch through 6mm steel truck doors without fragmenting.

An armorer melted fifty pounds of scavenged low-temperature silver-cadmium brazing wire in an unventilated casting pot. Yellow cadmium oxide fumes filled the workshop; the caster suffered acute chemical pneumonitis and pulmonary edema forty-eight hours later.

Adding 4% scrap pewter tankard metal (92% Sn) reduced molten surface tension dramatically. The alloy completely filled micro-fine grease grooves and sharp driving bands on multi-cavity gang molds, cutting reject rates from 35% down to 2%.
